name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to help keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks without cluttering the interface for mouse users. The trade-off is one extra DOM element, but it’s invisible to sighted mouse users and solves a critical keyboard navigation barrier.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it’s hidden until focus—if it blends into the page or lacks visual emphasis, they’ll never discover it. A better alternative is a permanently visible skip link styled as a small, high-contrast button in the top-left corner, sacrificing minimal screen space for guaranteed discoverability. Settle it with user testing: track how often keyboard users activate the skip link before and after the change.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users treating the skip link as visual noise—if it’s always visible but blends into the page, it becomes ignored, defeating its purpose. A better alternative is a skip link that appears only when tabbed to, but with a strong visual cue (e.g., a bright outline or animated pulse) to ensure discovery without permanent clutter. Settle it with user testing: track if keyboard users can find and use it within 3 seconds.
